## Natural history notes

A large tree-perching duck characterized by a long neck, bright pink bill, gray face, chestnut breast, black belly, white wing patches, and long pink legs. In Florida, the Black-bellied Whistling-Duck is found in freshwater marshes, ponds, lakes, wetlands, flooded fields, golf-course ponds, stormwater basins, and agricultural areas, often gathering in noisy flocks. It feeds mainly on seeds, grasses, grains, and aquatic vegetation, and nests in tree cavities, nest boxes, or occasionally on the ground near wetlands.
